Tips for job search in Finland: 

You can find tips for finding a job in Finland on the Public Employment Service’s Job Market Finland. 

Many company websites in Finland are also in English and you can find open vacancies and application forms there. Once you have found a vacancy that interests you, make sure you submit a job application that meets the requirements stated in the ad. Generally, the length of the application/cover letter is one page and the CV max. two pages. You can use, for instance, Home | Europass to create your CV and cover letter. 

You can also directly contact and send your CV to companies in Finland even if they do not have open vacancies at the moment. We recommend you research potential companies in the sectors that you are interested in and confidently establish contact with the right contact person. 

Social media can also be a powerful tool in job search. In some fields LinkedIn is the main recruitment channel and creating a LinkedIn profile can increase your chances of finding a job. It is also a good idea to join regional job-search groups, for instance, on Facebook. 

Entrepreneurship: 

If you are thinking about starting a business in Finland, you can find information and services on the Suomi.fi website.

There are also 30 Enterprise Agencies in Finland offering free and confidential business counselling to all interested in entrepreneurship.

Information for Jobseekers

Are you a jobseeker? Then welcome aboard! and…

... GET READY: register, apply and prepare to chat!

Follow the steps below to make the most of the event!

Jobseekers’ registration is now available.

1. Register & upload your CV

Make sure your profile stands out to employers:

  • Clearly describe your language, technical and soft skills, education, and work experience.
  • Upload your CV in English (use Europass if you still don’t have one).
  • Add a profile picture (optional, but recommended).

Need help? Watch this video on how to register and create your profile.

2. Apply for jobs & confirm interviews

Simply uploading your CV is not enough. You must apply for jobs to be visible to employers.

  • Browse the platform and apply for positions matching your skills and experience.
  • Employers may invite you to one or more online interviews on the event day – 15th of September or in the week following the event.
  • If pre-selected, you will receive a notification with available interview slots — please reply as soon as possible.
  • Already applied? Check your Dashboard under My job applications for interview invitations. Confirm acceptance and choose most convenient time slots for you.

Here’s how to apply for a job and confirm an interview.

3. Prepare for interviews

Good preparation makes all the difference. Here’s how to get ready:

  • Research participating companies: their activities, values, and current vacancies.
  • Decide which employers you want to approach and prepare your own questions.
  • Anticipate possible interview questions and practice your answers.
  • Make a professional impression: dress appropriately (even if online).
  • Always stay positive.
  • English is the main working language, so aim for clarity and confidence.

Before your interview, make sure you have:

  • A PC, laptop, tablet/iPad, or similar device
  • A headset with microphone and a webcam
  • A stable internet connection

Once your interview is confirmed, the employer will be waiting for you at the agreed time. If on the platform, login, go to My job applications and click on Join interview.

4. Join the Live Chat on 15th of September

You will be able to:

  • Chat directly with employers about job opportunities.
  • Receive advice from EURES Advisers on working and living in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Norway, Slovenia, Spain and Sweden.
5. Follow the Programme
  • Take full advantage of the live-streamed programme on 15th of September.
  • Select the presentations that interest you.
  • Watch live sessions and ask questions to the speakers via open chat.
We look forward to welcoming you online on 15th of September 2026.
Good luck with your job search!

Information for Non-EU/EFTA Nationals

Dear candidate,

If you are a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA, we kindly inform you that this event is currently only open to EU/EEA residents. However, we understand you may be interested in opportunities to live and work in Europe in the future.

The information provided below will give you an overview of work permit requirements in Austria, France, Germany, Italy, Norway, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden. Please read it carefully before you decide to apply for jobs in any of these 8 countries.

Special conditions apply (such as a Temporary Protection Status) if you are an Ukrainian citizen currently fleeing from the war. Please check further info HERE...

 

  • Austria

Dear Ladies & Gentlemen,

Thank you very much for your interest in a job and your inquiry regarding living and working in Austria. You can find all the requirements for third-country nationals to live and work in Austria on the Austrian government's migration platform here.

As a foreign employee, you can contact ABA – Invest in Austria (WORK in AUSTRIA) at https://www.workinaustria.com/ for support and guidance through the Red-White-Red Card process. Additionally, you can find all the necessary information and contact options here.

We wish you much success in your future endeavors.

Sincerely,

EURES National Coordination Office Austria

 

  • France

If you are not a citizen of the EU/EEA or Switzerland:

Please keep in mind that, although you can participate in this event and use European Job Days platform for job searching and meeting employers, you will have to comply with additional legal obligations and administrative procedures to access the European labour market.

We advise you to find out in advance for further information:

  • the basic principles of access to the European labour market for individual third-country nationals,
  • the European immigration portal.

You should also be aware that employers may decide not to proceed with your application due to the expected length of immigration procedures related to your employment.

 

  • Germany

Working in Germany: step by step.

You are interested in working or undergoing a vocational training programme in Germany? We explain the requirements and what you need to do – step by step.

We support you.

You do not yet live in Germany? You would like to find a job or undergo a vocational training programme in Germany? The Federal Employment Agency can help you. Make use of our support – reliable, personal and free of charge:

Please download the registration form here and send it together with your current CV in a single email to zav@arbeitsagentur.de with the subject "Seize the winter".

 

  • Italy

If you are a non-EU worker resident in Italy, you can work in Italy only if you have a valid residence permit that entitles you to work.

As a non-EU citizen, you can live and work in Italy through several specific visa pathways: securing an employer-sponsored job (via the Decreto Flussi quota), working as a remote digital nomad, launching a startup, or obtaining a student visa. All pathways require a valid Permesso di Soggiorno (residence permit). This applies to all foreign citizens who are not from an EU country, whether they are refugees, asylum seekers or under international protection.

(A visa is a document that is required to enter Italy. It therefore allows you to legally enter the country. A residence permit, which you must apply for upon entering Italian territory, is the document required to legally reside in Italy.)

Non-EU citizens wishing to work as an employed worker in Italy will find information below on the conditions to fulfil and procedures to follow, as well as the rights they can enjoy during their stay:
o EU Immigration Portal - Employed worker in Italy
o Foreigners in Italy | Cliclavoro
o Non-EU workers | Cliclavoro
o Entry and residence visa into Italy
o Tax identification number for foreign citizens

You are welcome to explore job opportunities in Italy through the EURES Portal.

For additional guidance on employment for non-EU nationals, please visit:  
o Who are the "digital nomads"? How can they enter Italy?
o Residence permit for scientific research: how to get one and what does it grant

The ‘EU Blue Card’ may be issued to highly skilled non-EU workers. It is an entry scheme that allows for the recruitment of highly skilled workers from abroad, outside the quotas set by the immigration quota decree. 
o Highly qualified worker
o La carta blue UE

 

  • Norway

Non-EU nationals

EURES in Norway is not involved in the recruitment and placement of non-EU nationals. But you are free to look up jobs and information on the EURES portal.

Non-EU nationals need a residence permit before starting to work in Norway. The term work covers all types of jobs or commercial activities in Norway, paid or unpaid. More information on New in Norway, the official guide Residence permit in Norway | Ny i Norge.

 

  • Slovenia

This event is primarily designed for citizens of EU/EFTA countries.

If you are a citizen of a non-EU/EFTA country, we kindly inform you that you are not eligible to participate in this event. To work in Slovenia, non-EU/EFTA nationals need a valid residence and work permit, which requires a confirmed job offer from a Slovenian employer.

You are welcome to explore job opportunities in Slovenia through the EURES Portal.

For additional guidance on employment for non-EU nationals, visit Employment of Non-EU Migrant Workers.

 

  • Spain

If you are not a national of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway or Switzerland of a family member of a citizen of one of these countries you should get  a work permit to live and work in Spain. You could ask for information in the Spanish Embassy or consulate in your country.

In addition you can find useful information on the official link.

In general, a non European citizen previously to apply for a position should get a work permit and later apply for the position.

However, there are some situations in which non European citizens living abroad may work in Spain without needing to apply for a work permit - check here.

Some situations:
- Nationals from Peru and Chile (bilateral agreements)
- Foreign citizens who apply for occupations with labor shortage in Spain (If you applied for a labor shortage occupation then the employer could deal with the work permit needed, check here)

 

  • Sweden

As a citizen of a non-EU/-EEA country you are required to have a work-permit to work in Sweden. To apply for a work-permit, a definite job offer from an employer in Sweden must have been presented to you. The Swedish Migration Agency-Migrationsverket- offers more information about work permit and working in Sweden.

For more information go here.

You can find more about work in Sweden here.

For more guidance about the possibilities for non-EU/EEA citizens, please visit the website of your country of interest:

On the day of the event you’ll have the opportunity to communicate with employers via individual online chats and listen to presentations about living and working conditions in Poland accompanied by public online chats.

 

WE ARE LOOKING FORWARD TO SEEING YOU ON 29th SEPTEMBER 2026!

Information for Non-EU/EFTA Nationals

If you are a citizen of a country outside the EU/EEA, we kindly inform you that this event is currently only open to EU/EEA residents. However, we understand you may be interested in opportunities to live and work in Europe in the future.

If you are interested in taking up employment in Poland, please note that third-country nationals can work in Poland, if they have a valid work permit or another document entitling them to work, or if they are an exempt from the obligation to have such a permit. In addition, every foreigner residing in Poland must have a valid residence permit.

As a rule, your future employer will arrange the work permit on your behalf. A foreigner,
on the other hand, arranges the right of residence at the Polish representation (embassy or consulate) in their home country or in the country where they are legally staying.

Special conditions apply in Poland if you are an Ukrainian citizen currently fleeing from the war. Please check further information. 

The following information may also be useful:

The EURES network assists exclusively jobseekers from the 27 European Union Member States, as well as Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Switzerland. If you are a resident of another country, we unfortunately can't help you.

Information for employers

Are you having difficulties finding suitable employees?
Time for a solution that knows no borders!
Take part in the Job and Entrepreneurship Fair 2026!

This year's edition will combine a traditional job fair with the European Online Job Day, enabling Polish employers to present job offers on a European scale and establish contacts with candidates from EU/EEA countries and Polish jobseekers returning from abroad.

For over twenty years, the Job and Entrepreneurship Fair has been the largest and one of the most important events dedicated to labour market issues in Warsaw and the Masovian region. This event is a recognized forum for cooperation between public institutions, employers, organisations supporting entrepreneurship, and labour market experts. The purpose of the venture is to support professional mobility, promote employment, and create a space for direct contact between employers and jobseekers.

European Job Days are Europe-wide online job fairs that connect jobseekers and employers from various European member states.

This event is an excellent opportunity to promote vacancies in your company across Europe.

By taking part in the event, you have the chance to recruit candidates with the desired qualifications and various language competences.

By registering an Employer account, you can manage the advertisements and recruitment projects posted there.

On September 29 of this year from 10:00 to 17:00 you will have the opportunity to talk to candidates through individual online chats. Participation in the fair is free of charge.

On the EJD website select the event Job and Entrepreneurship Fair 2026, click the yellow registration tile for this event, and then create a new account. Next, select "I am an employer" and fill in all mandatory fields. If you still have doubts about how to register, watch the tutorial here.

The account will be activated after your details are checked by the organisers, which may take 1-2 days. After positive verification, you will receive a link to activate your account.

Then, after logging in, you can check what opportunities the platform offers in terms of presenting your company and scheduling candidates for interviews!

The company description and the content of advertisements should be published in English. If necessary, content in another language, e.g. Polish, may be added to the text in English.

Please remember that individual interviews with candidates on the day of the fair using a webcam/headset or traditional text chat will increase your chances of acquiring the best candidates!

The registration deadline for Polish employers is 15 September of this year.

We cordially invite YOU!

  1. This event is strictly dedicated to Polish employers wanting to recruit jobseekers from EU/EEA countries, particularly Polish returnees. The organisers will not accept employers from any other countries.
  2. The online event is organised by the Voivodeship Labor Offices in Warsaw, Kielce, Toruń, Rzeszów, and Zielona Góra.
  3. The on-site event takes place on 29 September 2026 at PGE Narodowy in Warsaw and is organised in partnership with the Voivodeship Labor Office in Warsaw, the Labor Office of the Capital City of Warsaw, and the Economic Development Bureau of the Capital City of Warsaw. If your company wants to participate in it - pleas fill in the on-line application for at: https://www.up.warszawa.pl/targi/

Informacje dla pracodawców

Masz trudności ze znalezieniem odpowiednich pracowników?
Czas na rozwiązanie, które nie zna granic!
Weź udział w Targach Pracy i Przedsiębiorczości 2026!

Tegoroczna edycja połączy tradycyjne targi pracy z Europejskim Dniem Pracy Online, umożliwiając polskim pracodawcom prezentację ofert zatrudnienia w skali europejskiej oraz nawiązywanie kontaktów z kandydatami z krajów UE/EOG, w tym z Polakami chcącymi powrócić z zagranicy.

Targi Pracy i Przedsiębiorczości od ponad dwudziestu lat stanowią największe i jedno z najważniejszych wydarzeń poświęconych zagadnieniom rynku pracy w Warszawie oraz w regionie mazowieckim. Wydarzenie to jest uznanym forum współpracy instytucji publicznych, pracodawców, organizacji wspierających przedsiębiorczość oraz ekspertów rynku pracy. Celem przedsięwzięcia jest wspieranie mobilności zawodowej, promocja zatrudnienia oraz tworzenie przestrzeni do bezpośredniego kontaktu pracodawców z osobami poszukującymi pracy.

Europejskie Dni Pracy to ogólnoeuropejskie internetowe targi pracy, które łączą osoby poszukujące pracy i pracodawców z różnych europejskich państw członkowskich.

To wydarzenie jest doskonałą okazją do promowania wolnych miejsc pracy w Twojej firmie w całej Europie.

Biorąc udział w wydarzeniu, masz szansę rekrutować kandydatów z pożądanymi kwalifikacjami i różnymi kompetencjami językowymi.

Poprzez rejestrację konta Wystawcy możesz zarządzać zamieszczonymi tam ogłoszeniami i projektami rekrutacyjnymi. 29 września tego roku od 10:00 do 17:00 będziesz mieć możliwość rozmawiania z kandydatami poprzez indywidualne czaty online. Udział w targach jest bezpłatny.

Na stronie internetowej EJD wybierz wydarzenie "Job and Entrepreneurship Fair 2026", kliknij żółty kafelek rejestracji dla tego wydarzenia, a następnie utwórz nowe konto. Następnie wybierz „Jestem pracodawcą” i wypełnij wszystkie obowiązkowe pola. Jeśli nadal masz wątpliwości, jak się zarejestrować, obejrzyj samouczek tutaj.

Konto zostanie aktywowane po sprawdzeniu Twoich danych przez organizatorów, co może zająć 1-2 dni. Po pozytywnej weryfikacji otrzymasz link do aktywacji swojego konta.

Następnie, po zalogowaniu się, możesz sprawdzić, jakie możliwości oferuje platforma w zakresie prezentowania Twojej firmy i umawiania kandydatów na rozmowy kwalifikacyjne!

Opis firmy oraz treść ogłoszeń powinny być opublikowane w języku angielskim. W razie potrzeby treść w innym języku, np. polskim, może być dodana do tekstu w języku angielskim.

Prosimy pamiętać, że indywidualne rozmowy z kandydatami w dniu targów przy użyciu kamerki/słuchawek lub tradycyjnego czatu tekstowego zwiększą Twoje szanse na pozyskanie najlepszych kandydatów!

Termin rejestracji dla polskich pracodawców to 15 września tego roku.

  1. To wydarzenie jest dedykowane ściśle polskim pracodawcom chcącym rekrutować osoby poszukujące pracy z krajów UE/EOG, w szczególności Polaków chcących powrócić z zagranicy. Organizatorzy nie przyjmą pracodawców z żadnych innych krajów.
  2. Wydarzenie w formule online jest organizowane przez Wojewódzkie Urzędy Pracy w Warszawie, Kielcach, Toruniu, Rzeszowie i Zielonej Górze.

Online Recruitment Event – Announcement

EURES Slovenia Connects: Work Opportunities Await

Your next career step within the European labour market may lead you to Slovenia.

Save the date: 15 October 2026 | 11:00–13:30 (CET)
Hybrid event: Maribor, Slovenia

The Online Job Fair “EURES Slovenia Connects: Work Opportunities Await” will facilitate recruitment and labour mobility by connecting jobseekers from across Europe with Slovenian and European employers operating in a wide range of economic sectors.

Slovenia currently records high labour demand and low unemployment, creating strong conditions for international recruitment and sustainable employment. The event will provide participants with direct access to:

  • Slovenian employers and their job opportunities
  • European employers, represented by national EURES Advisers
  • EURES services, including information on recruitment conditions, mobility support, and living and working conditions in Slovenia

In addition to employer engagement, jobseekers will receive structured information on labour market opportunities, employment conditions, and integration into the Slovenian working environment.

Whether you are an experienced specialist or at an early stage of your career journey, this event offers a valuable opportunity to explore employment options and establish direct contact with employers and EURES representatives.

Further information:
EURES Slovenia – eures@ess.gov.si

About this event

Your Future – Made in Germany. Your next chapter begins here!

Are you ready to turn your professional goals into reality? Germany is more than just a place to work—it is a place to grow, innovate, and thrive.

Join us on 28 October 2026 online for Make it in Germany – Take Your Chance and take the next step toward your dream career. This exclusive event is your backstage pass to the German labour market. Connect directly with leading employers, gain valuable insights into the recognition of your qualifications, and navigate the application process with confidence.

We are looking for trailblazers in:

  • Healthcare: Doctors, nurses, and medical specialists
  • Tech & Innovation: IT experts and digital visionaries
  • Service & Hospitality: Professionals for world-class hotels and tourism
  • Engineering & Skilled Trades: Technicians, electricians, and metalworkers
  • Education: Passionate kindergarten teachers and educators
  • Logistics: Reliable truck and bus drivers

Don’t just watch the future happen—be part of it.

Please download the registration form here and send it together with your current CV in a single email to: take-your-chance@arbeitsagentur.de.

Once we have reviewed your documents, we will get back to you with further information.

About this event

For the sixth time, we cordially invite you to discover the recruitment and career opportunities in the border region – with valuable insights, practical tips and real-life experiences!

Please note that this event will be held in Dutch and German and is dedicated to the German-Dutch cross-border Employers only.

Gain valuable insights into cross-border recruitment and working conditions, discover cultural differences and similarities between Germany and the Netherlands, and benefit from the experiences of regional employers.

Event for jobseekers and employees + opportunity for live chat with advisors from the EURES Team Rhine-Waal

At this event, you can expect practical information and personal insights into working in the neighbouring country. Learn more about the cultural differences and similarities between Germany and the Netherlands. Benefit from practical tips on job applications: What do you need to bear in mind when applying for a job in the Netherlands? What are the dos and don'ts in the neighbouring country? DISCLAIMER

This event is for EU & EFTA citizens only and aimed at employers and jobseekers residing in the cross-border region between Netherlands and Germany.

Our team and affiliated organisations are unable to offer support for residents of countries outside the European Union/European Economic Area in finding work, including temporary or seasonal work.

The border between Norway and Sweden is the longest border in Europe, with its 1600 kilometers and we guide people about living and working across the border

Norway and Sweden offer a lot of job opportunities in many sectors – for example, the oil and gas industry, the health sector, hospitality, tourism, the fish industry, etc

We offer good living conditions and beautiful nature with a great work-life balance.

Today we will present some opportunities in our countries.

Information till utställare / Information for exhibitors (SE)

Swedish Day är ett rekryterings event online där du som arbetsgivare erbjuds att, helt kostnadsfritt, möta och rekrytera kvalificerade kandidater från samtliga EU/EES länder. 

Eventet anordnas av Arbetsförmedlingen Eures på online-plattformen European Online Job Days.  

 

I vårt paket ingår följande: 

  • En digital monter på event portalen där du presenterar ditt företag och 
  • Annonserar lediga tjänster, kandidater söker utannonserad tjänster löpande, från dagen du publicerar och fram till veckan efter eventdagen. 
  • Träffar sökande i grupp under minst 10 minuter på eventdag, där du informerar om verksamheten, lediga tjänster samt tar emot och svarar på frågor från kandidater. Träffen sker genom plattformen, online. 
  • Intervjua kandidater som sökt en ledig tjänst hos dig, dessa kan du välja att intervjua vid valfritt tillfälle. 

Låter det intressant?  
Registrera ditt deltagande redan idag. En tidig anmälan ger ökad synlighet, fler kandidater och större chans att tillsätta din tjänst redan innan eventet äger rum. 

Annonsering 

Publicera era annonser på eventplattformen så snart som möjligt för att maximera synligheten och nå fler kandidater. 

För bästa matchning ska annonserna tydligt beskriva arbetsuppgifter och kvalifikationer samt vara skrivna på engelska. Har ni flera tjänster inom olika yrkesområden kan de samlas i en gemensam annons. 

Ni kan länka till företagets karriärsida, men eftersom kandidaterna söker via eventplattformen är det viktigt att ni loggar in regelbundet och följer upp inkomna ansökningar. 

 

Boka online intervjuer 

Plattformen erbjuder en intervjufunktion, men ni väljer själva vilket intervjuverktyg ni vill använda. Genomför gärna intervjuer löpande i takt med att ansökningarna kommer in och informera kandidaterna om detta i era annonser. 

 

Efter du har registrerat din medverkan kommer vi att kontakta dig då vi berättar mer om upplägget och hur du på bästa sätt förbereder dig inför event dagen. 
För mer information om registrering, hur du publicerar annonser och övriga funktioner klicka här Du kan också kontakta oss på european-jobdays@arbetsformedlingen.se eller höra av dig till din kontaktperson så hjälper vi dig vidare!

Information for visitors

In order to get the most of this event, you should:

  • Improve your profile / CV
    Pay attention to your language, technical or soft skills, as well as educational fields. If you haven’t done so yet, we strongly advise you to have your CV uploaded in English or have it retrieved from the EURES portal. You can as well add your LinkedIn profile or any online portfolio. 
     
  • Apply for jobs & confirm your attendance to interviews
    There will be plenty of jobs waiting for you on the platform. Browse through these vacancies and apply as soon as possible to those matching your skills and expectations. Uploading your CV is not enough, the employer can only view your profile/ CV when you apply for their jobs.

Companies may also invite you for one or more online interviews, to take place before, on or after the event day.

In case you are pre-selected, you will get a notification by the employer(s) and possible time suggestions for interview(s), to which you should answer as quickly as possible.
 

On the event day

On the event day, you can attend live presentations from the companies and be able to meet and listen to the employers and ask your questions.

You will be able to post your questions in the general chat that will be offered on the event-page.

You can also watch us live, learning more about Sweden and the participating employers and what opportunities there will be for you.

 

Prepare for the interview(s)
In order to better prepare, you should thoroughly research available information on the participating companies their main projects and recruitment needs. Select the companies you want to approach, identify the questions you may want to ask and try to anticipate possible questions from the employer.

A cared personal look is important (even if the interview is online) and a good level of English combined with a positive attitude, will prove highly beneficial.

Please make sure, ahead of the day of an online interview, you have access to:

  • PC, laptop, tablet / iPad or another mobile device plus a headset with a microphone and a webcam.
  • a stable internet connection

 

If you are not an EU/EEA or Swiss citizen

Please bear in mind that, while you may participate in this event and use the www.europeanjobdays.eu platform for job search and meeting employers, you will still have additional legal obligations and administrative procedures to go through to get access to the European labour market.

You should also be aware that employers may decide not to go through your application, due to the expected length of immigration procedures related to your hiring.
